 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10-03-2017 the petitioner and his sister Smt. Sharada and her daughter Sumathi had been to B.R. Hills from Bengaluru by hiring a Toyota Etios-GD car bearing Reg.
No. KA-04-D-8810.

Next day on 11-03-2017, when they were going to K. Gudi in the said car, in between B.R. Hills and K. Gudi road, Chamarajnagar, (between Biligiri Rangana Betta and Kyathadevara Gudi road, Chamarajnagar), within the jurisdiction of Chamarajanagar East Police Station, the driver of the said car drove the same in high speed and in rash & negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and lost control over the said vehicle and dashed to roadside rock situated in curve of hills and caused accident.
As a result the petitioner and other inmates of the vehicle suffered grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Ortho Clinic Hospital, Chamarajnagar, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter, he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery.
Earlier to the accident, the petitioner was working as employee at Toyota Kirloskar Motor Pvt. Ltd., Bidadi Industrial Area, Ramanagar District and was getting salary of Rs.65,000/- per month.
But, due to the above accidental injuries, the petitioner has became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The Chamarajnagar East Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow Lohith.K vs Ravi Prasad.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98545015/
2 the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.

sentences.text: 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Toyota Etios-GD car bearing No. KA-04-D-8810.
It has contended that the said car was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate as such it is not liable for payment of any compensation as claimed by the claimant.
It has denied the age, avocation and income, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 11-03-2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Toyota Etios-GD car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-D- 8810 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

3 . What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked 31 documents as Ex.P.1 to 31.

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Nagaraj B.N.,
as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

9. Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 10-03-2017 the petitioner and his sister Smt. Sharada and her daughter Sumathi had been to B.R. Hills from Bengaluru by hiring a Toyota Etios-GD car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-D-8810.

Next day on 11-03-2017, when they were going to K.
Gudi in the said car, in between B.R. Hills and K. Gudi road, Chamarajnagar, (between Biligiri Rangana Betta and Kyathadevara Gudi road, Chamarajnagar), within the jurisdiction of Chamarajanagar East Police Station, the driver of the said car drove the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over the said vehicle and dashed to roadside rock and caused accident.
As a result the petitioner and other inmates of the vehicle suffered grievous injuries.
Due to the above accidental injuries, the petitioner has became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 31 documents as Ex.P.1 to 31.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is first information statement, Ex.P.3 is charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is statement of witness, Ex.P.5 is spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is sketch, Ex.P.7 is Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.8 is wound certificate, Ex.P.9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is the certified copy of the R.C., Ex.P.11 is certified copy of the insurance policy, Ex.P.12 is certified copy of the driving licence,
Ex.P.13 is certified copy of the permit, Ex.P.14 is case-sheet, Ex.P.15 is X-ray, Ex.P.16 is relieve letter, Ex.P.17 is payment of gratuity letter, Ex.P.18 is service letter, Ex.P.19 is final settlement report, Ex.P.20 is show cause notice, Ex.P.21 is charge-sheet cum show cause notice, Ex.P.22 is reply, Ex.P.23 is charge-sheet cum show cause notice, Ex.P.24 is enquiry notice, Ex.P.25 is show cause notice, Ex.P.26 is reply, Ex.P.27 is authorization letter, Ex.P.28 are In-Patient records (total 2), Ex.P.29 is notarised copy of aadhar card, Ex.P.30 is Form No.16 for the assessment year of 2017-18 along with certificate U/Sec.65B of Evidence Act and Ex.P.31 are pay slips for the month of March-2017, April-2017, May-2017, June-2017, January-2019 and May- 2019 along with certificate U/sec.65B of Evidence Act.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, on 10-03- 2017 the petitioner and his sister Smt. Sharada and her daughter Sumathi had been to B.R. Hills from Bengaluru in a Toyota Etios-GD car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-D-8810.

Next day on 11-03-2017, when they were going to K. Gudi in the said car, in between B.R. Hills and K. Gudi road,
Chamarajnagar, the driver of the said car drove the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over the said vehicle and dashed to roadside rock and caused accident.
As a result the petitioner and other inmates of the vehicle suffered grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Toyota Etios- GD car bearing No. KA-04-D-8810 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of his body.
12. The petitioner, who has been examined as P.W.1, has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
The said facts have remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, though the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and in the cross-examination of P.W.1., it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and Lohith.K vs Ravi Prasad.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98545015/
4 documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner. Further, it is pertinent to note that, no where in the cross-examination of P.W.1, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has suggested that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing No. KA-04- D-8810.

With respect to other contentions taken in the written statement, though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

13. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.14 case- sheet, Ex.P.15 X-ray film and Ex.P.28 In-patient records, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered displaced communited fracture of the left humerus.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, on 12-03-2017, the petitioner was brought to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, with the history of road traffic accident and on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner had sustained displaced communited fracture of the left humerus and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nail.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Toyota Etios-GD car bearing No. KA-04-D-8810 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
14.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no other vehicle involved in the accident, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.3, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-D-8810.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of driver of offending car.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
17.

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 11-03-2017 at about 3.45 p.m. to 4.00 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car Toyota Etios-GD bearing No.KA- 04-D-8810.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Toyota Etios-GD car bearing No. KA-04-D-8810 and he has sustained displaced communited fracture of the left humerus and for the said injuries he has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the copy of his driving licence, which is marked as Ex.P.29.
As per Ex.P.29, the year of birth of the petitioner is 1978.
The accident has taken place on 11-03-2017.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 39 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered displaced communited fracture of the left humerus and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nail.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 32% physical disability of left arm and for the whole body he has 11%
physical disability.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.14 case-sheet, Ex.P.15 X-ray film and Ex.P.28 In-Patient records, clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered displaced communited fracture of the left humerus and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nail.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the Ex.P.28 document is not related to the petitioner, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the Lohith.K vs Ravi Prasad.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98545015/
6 P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 11-03-2017 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 22-08-2022, which is after lapse of five years and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, left humerus shows united humerus fracture.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the physical disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as employee at Toyota Kirloskar Motor Pvt. Ltd., Bidadi Industrial Area, Ramanagar District and was getting salary of Rs.65,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

To substantiate the same he has produced releave letter, payment of gratuity letter, service letter, final settlement report, Form 16 for the assessment year of 2017-18 along with certificate U/sec. 65B of Evidence Act and pay slips for the month of March- 2017, April-2017, May-2017, June-2017, January-2019 and May-2019 along with certificate U/sec. 65B of Evidence Act, which are marked as Ex.P.16 to 19,
Ex.P.30 and 31.

From these documents it is clear that the petitioner was working as employee at Toyota Kirloskar Motor Pvt. Ltd., and as on the date of accident he was drawing gross salary of Rs.
65,437/- per month.

But, it is pertinent to note that, no where in the petition or in his evidence the petitioner has stated the nature of his work in the said company and due to injuries sustained in the accident he is not in a position to perform the said work.
b) Further it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, from the date of accident till 2019 he was the employee of Toyota Kirloskar Motor Private Limited Company.

The Ex.P.31 pay slips for the month of March- 2017, April-2017, May-2017,
June-2017, January-2019 and May-2019, produced by the petitioner himself, clearly speaks that,
even after accident the petitioner has attended his job and has received the salary regularly from his employer/company
. Further the Ex.P.16 relieving letter clearly speaks that, the petitioner has voluntarily resigned from his job.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he was not in a position to attend his regular work and continue with his regular job at Toyota Kirloskar Motor Private Limited Company and for the said reason he had opted to resign from his job.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, it can safely be held that, the petitioner has not sustained any loss of future income due to injuries and disability suffered by him in the alleged accident.

Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by the petitioner in the road traffic accident does not arise at all.
For the disability suffered by him, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charges.

But, he Lohith.K vs Ravi Prasad.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98545015/
7 has not produced any medical bills or prescriptions to establish the same.

sentences.text: Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
displaced communited fracture of the left humerus.

As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 05 days from 12-03-2017 to 16-03-2017, in Sparsh Hospital,
Bengaluru.
He has also underwent surgery i.e., (CRIF) closed reduction with internal fixation with nail.
Further as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 05 days from 12-03-2017 to 16-03-2017, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 5 = Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 05 days from 12-03-2017 to 16-03-2017, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, he might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 5 = Rs.4,000/-
is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Canara Bank Colony, Nagarabhavi road,
Bengaluru, the accident has taken place at B.R. Hills and K. Gudi road, Chamarajnagar and he has taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 5 days as inpatient at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, from the date of accident till 2019 he was the employee of Toyota Kirloskar Motor Private Limited.

Further, the Ex.P.31 pay slips for the month of March-2017, April-2017, May-2017, June-2017, January-2019 and May-2019, produced by the petitioner himself, clearly speaks that, even after accident the petitioner has received the salary regularly from his employer/company and he has not suffered any loss of income during the period of treatment.
Hence, granting compensation for loss of income during the treatment period does not arise in the instant case.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

viii) Loss of amenities: It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 39 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.

8 ix)
Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture is united and implants are removed.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses Nil 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 5,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 4,000-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during Nil treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 93,000-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.93,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car Toyota Etios-GD bearing No.KA-04-D-8810 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.93,000/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.93,000/- (Rupees ninety three thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till Lohith.K vs Ravi Prasad.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98545015/
9 realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

 JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The Chamarajnagar East Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 11-03-2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Toyota Etios-GD car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-D- 8810 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3 . What order or Award ?
6.
Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 11-03-2017 at about 3.45 p.m. to 4.00 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car Toyota Etios-GD bearing No.KA- 04-D-8810.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Toyota Etios-GD car bearing No. KA-04-D-8810 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
14.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no other vehicle involved in the accident, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.3, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-D-8810.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of driver of offending car.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the physical disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by the petitioner in the road traffic accident does not arise at all.
For the disability suffered by him, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
Hence, granting compensation for loss of income during the treatment period does not arise in the instant case.
20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car Toyota Etios-GD bearing No.KA-04-D-8810 the accident has occurred.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.
19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses Nil 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 5,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 4,000-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during Nil treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 93,000-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.93,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.93,000/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.93,000/- (Rupees ninety three thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till Lohith.K vs Ravi Prasad.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98545015/
9 realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
